task_snapshot.issue: At the historical revision, lease ownership compares a database timestamp with the worker host clock. A host clock one year ahead rejects a valid lease. A host clock behind accepts an expired lease. Make database time authoritative without weakening owner and fencing-token checks.
task_snapshot.title: A worker clock rejects a valid database lease
task_snapshot.provenance: Historical controlled reproduction; clock uses a deterministic timestamp fixture.

summary: The proposed patch updates the database timestamp in the lease ownership check to be authoritative, while maintaining the owner and fencing-token checks. The change ensures that the database time is used for determining lease validity, preventing clock skew issues without compromising security.
